To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
transendocardial and transepicardical delivery of 125I-FGFF2 results in myocardial retention of 18% and 23%, respectively, with 2% and 12% at 7 d.

transendocardial and transepicardium intramyocardial injection of 125I-labeled FGF-2 in pigs results in efficient deposition and retention in the target tissue, and myocardial distribution is significantly greater than intracoronar, intrapericaridal, and intravenous injection.
transendocardial injection is more efficient than transvenous injection and is as efficient as transepicardium injection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the delivery of therapeutic proteins to the heart.
the development of a new method of drug delivery to the heart.
the development of a new method of myocardial gene therapy that is based on a combination of intramyocardial injection and electroporation of the heart muscle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
transendocardial and transepicardials are both effective delivery systems, and that transendocardially delivered FGF2 is more effective than intracoronarially delivered FGF-2.
transendocardial injection is superior to transepicardiial delivery in that the former allows for a more precise delivery of the therapeutic agent.
the transendocardial and transepicardal intramyocardial administration of 125I-FG2 results in myocardial deposition and distribution that are comparable with transepcardial delivery.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
transendocardial catheter-based delivery is a safe, efficient, and effective means for local delivery to the target myocardial area, with myocardial distribution limited to injection sites.
the transendocardial approach is superior to the transseptal approach for intramyocardial injection, and that transendocardial injection is superior to transcoronary injection.
transendocardial and transepicardinal IM injection of a therapeutic protein is a feasible approach for local delivery to the target tissue.
The main takeaway from our work is that
transendocardial injection of FGF2 results in efficient and sustained myocardial deposition of FGF2.
intracoronary administration of FGF2 results in a high degree of systemic exposure and very little retention within the myocardium.
transendocardial administration of FGF2 is a feasible method for myocardial gene transfer and that this technique can be used to deliver a wide range of therapeutic agents to the heart.
